excerpt: Base Code, from Base44, lets product, design, marketing and QA teams change an existing GitHub codebase in plain language from the browser, with a live preview and a normal pull request for engineers to review. What it does, requirements, pricing status and alternatives.
content:
Base Code is a browser-based workspace from Base44 for working on a codebase you already have. You connect a GitHub repository, describe a change in plain language, and Base Code makes it on an isolated branch with a live preview. When the change is ready, it goes to engineering as a standard GitHub pull request, so existing branch protections, required checks and review rules stay in place and engineers still decide what merges.

The pitch is that more of the team can contribute: product, design, marketing and QA as well as engineering. Nobody needs to clone the repository or set up a local development environment, and teammates can see each other's sessions and live previews and jump into any branch. GitHub stays the source of truth: Base Code commits and pushes to the working branch as you chat. It works with web and full-stack projects, keeps the project's own stack, and stores secrets encrypted across branches. The preview is for development only; you still release through your own hosting and deployment process.

Base Code launched on Product Hunt on 12 October 2026, Base44's ninth launch there, and finished #3 for the day with 196 upvotes. The footer of Base44's site credits Wix.com Ltd.

We have not tested Base Code ourselves. This page brings together Base44's Base Code page, documentation and pricing page, its Product Hunt launch and the official pricing pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.os: Browser; needs a web or full-stack project in a GitHub repository
profile.starts_at: Pricing not published for Base Code
profile.summary_short: Browser workspace where the whole team changes an existing GitHub codebase in plain language and ships through pull requests
use_cases: A product manager or designer fixing copy, layout or small features without waiting for an engineer
QA reproducing and fixing a bug on its own branch, then handing it over as a pull request
Marketing updating a landing page that lives in the product's codebase
Engineers reviewing teammates' changes with the same pull-request process they already use

fit: have an existing web or full-stack product in a GitHub repository
want non-engineers to contribute changes while engineering keeps code review and branch protections
don't want every contributor to set up a local development environment
not_fit: host your code on GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps: Base Code's documentation covers GitHub only
are building an app inside Base44's own app editor: the docs say to keep using the editor and its GitHub integration
want hosting for production: the preview is for development only
have a repository whose root project is not a web or full-stack app, such as a pure mobile app

pricing.intro: Pricing not published. Base44 does not list a price for Base Code on its Base Code page or in its documentation, and its pricing page does not say which Base44 plan includes it. For reference, Base44's general app-builder plans on 14 October 2026 were Free, Starter at $16, Builder at $40, Pro at $80 and Elite at $160 a month billed yearly, plus Enterprise.

plans.name: Base Code
plans.detail: No price or plan requirement is stated on the Base Code page or in the docs

notes: Base44's documentation mentions that a coupon code for Base Code can cover up to 10 people in a workspace.
Base44's plans can be cancelled or changed any time from account settings, taking effect at the next billing cycle. The pricing page does not state refund terms.

alternatives.intro: Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Builder.io
items.what: AI visual IDE that connects to your repository so teams can make code changes
items.starts_at: Free for 1 user; Pro $24 per user a month
items.difference: Connects to GitLab and Bitbucket as well as GitHub; Base Code's documentation covers GitHub only.

items.name: GitHub Copilot
items.what: GitHub's AI assistant, whose cloud agent can work on a repository and open pull requests
items.difference: Built for developers working in GitHub and their editor, without a shared live-preview workspace aimed at non-engineers.

items.name: Replit
items.what: Browser IDE with an AI agent that builds and hosts apps
items.difference: Also hosts and deploys apps; Base Code explicitly leaves production hosting to your own setup.

pros: Works on your existing codebase and stack; no migration to Base44's own platform
Changes arrive as standard GitHub pull requests, and branch protections and checks still apply
Isolated branches with live previews, visible to the whole team
GitHub remains the source of truth
cons: No published price, and no statement of which plan includes it
GitHub only, according to the docs
Web and full-stack projects only at the repository root
Opening a pull request needs GitHub write access; without it you work on a fork or copy

x.none: We found no independent posts about Base Code on X to link yet.

faq.q: How much does Base Code cost?
faq.a: Base44 has not published a price for Base Code, and its pricing page doesn't say which plan includes it. Base44's general plans run from free to $160 a month billed yearly, plus Enterprise.

faq.q: Does it work with my existing codebase?
faq.a: Yes, if it is a web or full-stack project in a GitHub repository. Base Code keeps your stack and doesn't add Base44's database, login or SDK.

faq.q: Do I need a local development environment?
faq.a: No. There is no cloning, dependency installation or local setup; everything runs in a shared cloud environment.
Engineering, through standard GitHub pull requests. Existing branch protections, required checks and review rules stay in place.

faq.q: What if I don't have write access to the repository?
faq.a: The project opens read-only. You can connect a public fork or private copy, and pull requests then target that copy.

faq.q: Can Base Code host my app in production?
faq.a: No. The live preview is for development; you release through your existing hosting and deployment process.
